title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Stochastic Analysis and Computational Methods
description:
About the position

A position as Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Stochastic Analysis and Computational Methods is available at Department of Mathematics, within the section of Risk and Stochastics.

Starting date no later than January 31st, 2027.

The appointment is a full-time position and is for a period of three years (10% of which is devoted to other career-promoting work, usually in the form of teaching activities). 

Depending upon the qualification of the applicant and the current needs of the department, a fourth year may be considered. In this case, a workload of 25% is devoted to career promoting work, usually in the form of teaching and/or supervision duties. In this case, Postdoctoral fellows who are appointed for a period of four years are expected to acquire basic pedagogical competency in the course of their fellowship period within the duty component of 25%.

No one can be appointed for more than one Postdoctoral Research Fellowship at the University of Oslo.

The position is bounded to the SURE-AI consortium agreement and its research scopes. The Centre for Sustainable, Risk-Averse, and Ethical AI or SURE-AI is a Norwegian AI centre funded by the Research Council of Norway (2025-2030). The primary objective is to create a new generation of algorithms for inference and decision-making by pushing the boundaries of the underlying computational techniques. SURE-AI researchers will drive a transformative leap in AI through a groundbreaking Centre initiative dedicated to making Artificial Intelligence more efficient, transparent and safe, addressing the critical challenges of resource consumption, behaviour unpredictability and ethical alignment with human and societal values. The centre involves senior researchers from well-renowned national and international research institutions, in close collaboration with industry and public sector. Overall, SURE-AI includes 19 national Norwegian partners, as well as researchers from 15 international institutions.

Six national research centres for Artificial Intelligence (AI) were launched in the Fall of 2025. These centres will foster interdisciplinary collaboration among researchers to address both scientific and societal challenges, develop new technologies, understand the impact of AI, and drive innovation across both the business and public sectors. This initiative is established and financed through the government's significant investment in artificial intelligence over the next five years

The present postdoctoral position is hosted at the Department of Mathematics, at Blindern campus in Oslo, which is the place of work.


Project description

The position is framed in the strongly interdisciplinary research group of Risk and Stochastics and the Community of SURE-AI. The focus is on the development of original mathematical methods for AI and its applications aimed at the modelling and analysis of complex phenomena particularly within economics and finance, energy finance, sustainable and ethical economics and insurance. 

We are interested in research projects that are deeply grounded in stochastic analysis and show also development of computational methods towards machine learning. The projects will focus on applications to risk-sensitive decision making and control, with the potential to address ethical and human alignment in machine learning research.

For this, candidates with a strong background in the areas of stochastic analysis, Malliavin calculus, forward and backward stochastic differential equations, signature methods, filtering, machine learning and computational stochastics are particularly welcome and are prioritized. Clear interest in computational methods towards applications is appreciated.

We are interested in candidates that can merge into an internationally oriented group with high ambitions in research excellency. It is expected that the fellow takes active part in both the research development and the group’s activities. 

The main purpose of a postdoctoral fellowship is to provide the candidates with enhanced skills to pursue a scientific top position within or beyond academia. To promote a strategic career path, all postdoctoral research fellows are required to submit a professional development plan no later than one month after commencement of the postdoctoral period.


What skills are important in this role?

The Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences has a strategic ambition to be among Europe’s leading communities for research, education and innovation. Candidates for these fellowships will be selected in accordance with this, and expected to be in the upper segment of their class with respect to academic credentials.

Required qualifications:

  • Applicants must hold a degree equivalent to a Norwegian doctoral degree in stochastic analysis, probability or mathematical statistics, numerical methods for stochastics, forward and/or backward stochastic differential equations, stochastic control, stochastic filtering. Doctoral dissertation must be submitted for evaluation by the closing date. Only applicants with an approved doctoral thesis and public defence are eligible for appointment.
  • Fluent oral and written communication skills in English.

Desired qualifications:

  • Interdisciplinary research experience and/or attitude in the relevant areas is an advantage. 
  • Knowledge of computational methods for stochastics and programming skills.
  • Knowledge in one or more of the following areas: Malliavin calculus, stochastic filtering, risk measures, signature methods.
  • Knowledge of a Scandinavian language may be an advantage for teaching and supervision (if applicable)

UiO is subject to the Security Act, which governs the organisation's protection of security-sensitive objects and knowledge, in addition to other relevant legislation concerning access to and handling of sensitive information. Based on this, it is a requirement that successful applicants are security-eligible. We may use background checks as part of our recruitment process.


What are we looking for in you?

Personal skills:

The fellow is expected to take part in the activities of the Section of Risk and Stochastics. We are expecting a person able to work in structured manner both independently and as part of a team, swiftly adapting to new tasks. In general, a positive attitude and the ability to handle hectic periods is an advantage. A genuine interest in taking part in the various aspects of the academic life with collaborative and pro-active attitude is highly appreciated. 
Good communication skills are important.

Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal skills.


We can offer you
  • Exciting and meaningful tasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing to knowledge development, education, and enlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, and knowledge-based societal development
  • Committed colleagues in a good working environment
  • Good welfare schemes.
  • Opportunity of up to 1.5 hours a week of exercise during working hours.  
  • A workplace with good development and career opportunities
  • Postdoctoral development programmes.
  • Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes with beneficial mortgages and good insurance schemes
  • Salary in position as Postdoctoral Fellow, position code 1352 in salary range NOK 595 000 - 690 000, depending on competence and experience. From the salary, 2 percent is deducted in statutory contributions to the State Pension Fund

We need different perspectives in our work

UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues, could you be the next one?

We will do our best to accommodate your needs. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps (Norwegian), we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports. More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here. 

We hope you will apply for the position with us.


How to apply

The application must include:

  • Cover letter (statement of motivation, summarizing scientific work and research interest)
  • Project description (no more than 3 pages, excluding references)
  • CV (summarizing education, positions, pedagogical experience, administrative experience and other qualifying activity)
  • Copies of educational certificates, academic transcript of records
  • A complete list of publications and up to 5 academic works that the applicant wishes to be considered by the evaluation committee
  • Names and contact details of 2-3 references (name, relation to candidate, e-mail and telephone number)

Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.


General information

The best qualified candidates will be invited for interviews.

Please see the guidelines and regulations for appointments to Postdoctoral fellowships at the University of Oslo.

If an applicant has applied for and been granted funding for a fulltime research stay abroad while being employed as a Postdoctoral Research Fellow, the employment will be prolonged with the equivalent time as the research stay, but for no longer than of twelve months ( thus extending the employment to a maximum of four years)

No one can be appointed twice as a Postdoctoral fellow financed with funds from The Research Council of Norway (NFR).

Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we can't, you will hear from us.

The University of Oslo has an agreement for all employees, aiming to secure rights to research results a.o.


Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest rated institution of research and education with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. Its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally esteemed research communities make UiO an important contributor to society. 

The Department of Mathematics is part of the Faculty of Mathematics and Natural Sciences at the University of Oslo. The Department is engaged in teaching and research covering a wide spectrum of subjects within mathematics, mechanics and statistics. The research is on theory, methods and applications. The areas represented include: fluid mechanics, biomechanics, statistics and data science, computational mathematics, combinatorics, partial differential equations, stochastics and risk, algebra, geometry, topology, operator algebras, complex analysis and logic.

We have almost 50 persons in permanent academic positions and a large number of post docs and Ph.D. students. We also have an administrative and technical staff. The department represents a leading research environment in mathematical areas in Norway, and has a highly international profile.

title: Bilklargjører søkes til Innlandet Bilutleie – 60 % stilling, førerkort klasse B kreves
description:
Vi søker en effektiv og pålitelig bilklargjører til vårt team i Gjøvik. Hos oss får du en variert og fysisk arbeidshverdag med klargjøring av leiebiler, og vi ser etter deg som liker å jobbe praktisk, effektivt og nøye. Erfaring er ikke nødvendig – opplæring gis.

Hva vi ser etter

Vi ser etter deg som er nøye, pålitelig og tar stolthet i arbeidet du gjør. En bil skal ikke bare se ren ut -- den skal være ordentlig klargjort og klar for neste kunde.

Du må være grundig og ha et godt øye for detaljer, både når det gjelder vask og når du kontrollerer bilen for skader eller andre avvik. Vi ser også etter deg som tar ansvar, jobber selvstendig og sier ifra dersom du oppdager noe som ikke er som det skal.

Du trenger ikke ha erfaring fra bilutleie eller bilpleie fra før. Det viktigste er at du er lærevillig, effektiv og opptatt av å gjøre en skikkelig jobb.

Arbeidsoppgaver

Innlandet Bilutleie søker bilvasker / bilklargjører i Gjøvik

Vi søker en pålitelig og effektiv medarbeider til vask og klargjøring av våre leiebiler.

Arbeidsdagen vil hovedsakelig bestå av:

  • Innvendig og utvendig vask av biler

  • Støvsuging og rengjøring

  • Klargjøring og enkel kontroll av biler før utleie

  • Flytting av biler og andre praktiske oppgaver knyttet til bilparken

Vi ser etter deg som:

  • Er pålitelig og møter til avtalt tid

  • Jobber effektivt og er opptatt av et godt resultat

  • Trives med fysisk arbeid og høyt tempo

  • Kan jobbe selvstendig, men også fungerer godt sammen med andre

  • Har førerkort klasse B -- dette er et krav

Tidligere erfaring med bilpleie eller klargjøring er en fordel, men ikke nødvendig. Du vil få nødvendig opplæring.

Stillingen er i utgangspunktet ca. 60 %, tilsvarende omtrent tre arbeidsdager i uken. Arbeidstid og konkrete dager avtales nærmere.

Vi ønsker en person som kan starte så snart som mulig.

Du trenger ikke skrive en lang søknad. Send oss noen korte ord om deg selv, når du kan starte og telefonnummeret ditt.

Arbeidssted: Gjøvik

Arbeidsgiver: Innlandet Bilutleie AS

Vi tilbyr

Hos Innlandet Bilutleie blir du en del av et lite og uformelt arbeidsmiljø med korte beslutningsveier og varierte arbeidsdager. Du får ansvar og tillit tidlig, samtidig som du får god opplæring i oppgavene.

Vi tilbyr:

  • Et hyggelig og uformelt arbeidsmiljø

  • Varierte arbeidsdager med praktiske oppgaver

  • God opplæring -- erfaring er ikke nødvendig

  • Selvstendig arbeid og ansvar

  • Mulighet til å lære mer om bil, bilutleie og drift

  • Forutsigbar deltidsstilling med mulighet for mer arbeid ved behov

  • Konkurransedyktige betingelser

Vi er en liten organisasjon der alle bidrar, og hvor det er kort vei fra idé til handling. For den rette personen kan det også være muligheter for mer ansvar og flere oppgaver over tid.

Om arbeidsgiveren:

Bilklargjører søkes til Innlandet Bilutleie -- 60 % stilling, førerkort klasse B kreves

title: Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Physics-Adapted Numerical Methods
description:
Postdoctoral Research Fellow in Physics-Adapted Numerical Methods

The Department of Computer Science, Electrical Engineering and Mathematical Sciences at Western Norway University of Applied Sciences, has a vacancy for a postdoctoral research fellow in numerical mathematics for a period of 3 years.
 
About the postdoctoral project:

The postdoctoral position is part of the project “Physics-Adapted Numerical Methods for Two-Phase Flow” (PANum) funded by the Research Council of Norway. The project is a joint collaboration between Western Norway University of Applied Sciences and Hasselt University in Belgium.

In PANum the goal is to formulate and implement mathematical methods that are not only robust, efficient and have a low numerical error, but that also guarantee that important physical properties are fulfilled in the numerical solution. Ultimately, PANum will lead to a computational algorithm that reliably simulates two-phase flow.

The postdoctoral project will be part of developing and analyzing relevant numerical methods and implement them in an open-source framework that will be made openly available for others to use. This will be relevant for example for CO2 storage and design of fuel cells. 


Research environment:

The PANum project is situated in the Engineering Computing research group at Western Norway University of Applied Sciences, and in the computational mathematics group (CMAT) at Hasselt University. Both groups focus strongly on numerical analysis and mathematical modelling. The prospective postdoctoral researcher will work in close collaboration with Carina Bringedal and Erlend Storvik from Engineering Computing, Jochen Schütz from CMAT, as well as the current PhD and master students connected to the PANum project.

 

Postdoctoral research fellows receive an annual work expense funding which can be used for conference participation, research visits, and equipment. The place of employment is campus Bergen or campus Førde. 


Qualifications:

Criteria for appointment to the position of postdoctoral fellow are regulated in Forskrift til universitets- og høyskoleloven.

Applicants must have earned a PhD degree in computer science, simulation science, applied mathematics or in a closely related field, or have submitted the PhD thesis before the application deadline. The PhD must have been awarded within 4 weeks after the application deadline. The scientific profile of qualified candidates must be within numerical methods for ODEs and PDEs.

 

A solid background in both the following fields is required:

  • Numerical analysis for ODEs and PDEs
  • Scientific programming using Python, MATLAB, C++, Julia, or similar

Furthermore, experience within:

  • collaborative code development and usage of version control tools like git
  • asymptotic methods, like two-scale asymptotic expansions or matched asymptotic expansions, for PDEs

will be considered an advantage when candidates are ranked. 

In addition to the required educational and scientific background, the following criteria will be evaluated:

  • Quality and relevance of PhD thesis
  • Quality and relevance of publications
  • Ability to work in intersection of theoretical and applied research
  • Ability to collaborate, lead the writing of research papers, ability to initiate and advance research, and research and scientific leadership potential
  • Oral and written good communication skills in English.

 

Career plan:

The person appointed shall, together with the institute, prepare a career plan that specifies the skills the postdoctoral researcher is to acquire. Competence goals shall be set both for the postdoctoral project and for any other career‑advancing work included in the position. The postdoctoral researcher will have access to career guidance.


Application procedure:

Applications will be evaluated by an expert panel of three members.

Applicants are asked to submit their application and CV online. Please use the link “Apply for this job” (“Søk stillingen”).

The following documentation should be uploaded as an attachment to the online application: 

  • A brief cover letter (max one page) including a description of research interests and motivation for working within the current project. The cover letter should include a detailed justification of your qualifications in relation to the listed requirements.
  • CV (summarizing education, positions and a complete list of academic publications)
  • PhD thesis
  • Transcripts and diplomas of bachelor’s, master’s and PhD degrees. If you have not yet been awarded your PhD degree, please submit a statement from your institution confirming the submission of the PhD thesis.
  • Copies of up to 5 selected academic publications
  • Names and contact details of 2 references (names, relation to candidate, email and telephone number).

Short-listed candidates might be required to give a research presentation, in addition to an interview. 

 

If the documents submitted are not in a Scandinavian language or in English, the applicants must submit certified translations of these. It is required that the applicant encloses a recognition document showing that their degree is equivalent to a Norwegian bachelor’s degree, master’s degree, or PhD. You can read more about applying for recognition of foreign higher education here.

 

The Norwegian Directorate for Higher Education and Skills (HK-dir) offers an automatic recognition document for certain degrees from selected countries. If the applicant’s degree is covered by the automatic recognition, it will be sufficient to attach this document. Read more about automatic recognition here.

 

As the HK-dir application process may take some time it is recommended to apply to HK-dir as soon as possible. If you have not received a recognition document from HK- dir within the application deadline, please enclose documentation from HK-dir showing that they have received your application.

 

Applicants should note that the evaluation will be based on the documentation submitted electronically via Jobbnorge within the submission deadline. The applicants are responsible for ensuring that all the documentation is submitted before the closing date. Applications cannot be sent by e-mail or to individuals at HVL.


Salary and benefits:

Exciting and stimulating work as part of a strong international academic environment.


An open and inclusive work environment with dedicated colleagues Favourable terms in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund.

The position as postdoctoral researcher is paid according to the Government's salary regulation, in position code 1352.


There is a compulsory 2 % deduction to the pension fund (see http://www.spk.no/en for more information). The successful applicant must comply with the guidelines that apply to the position at any time.


General information:

The appointment will be made in accordance with the regulations for State employees Law in Norway ("Lov om statens ansatte"). Organizational changes and changes in the duties and responsibilities associated with the position must be expected.

State employment shall reflect the multiplicity of the population at large to the highest possible degree. Western Norway University of Applied Sciences therefore aims to achieve a balanced age and gender composition and the recruitment of persons with diverse backgrounds.

Information about the applicants may be made public even though the applicant has requested not to be named in the list of applicants. The applicant will be notified if his/her request is not respected.

Short-listed applicants will be called in for an interview.

Employed on condition that you are granted a work and residence permit (must be considered individually).


Western Norway University of Applied Sciences is subjected to The Export Control Regulation. The regulation will be applied in the processing of the applications.


Contacts:

1) Professor Carina Bringedal, project leader of PANum

phone: +47 55 58 79 76, e-mail: carina.bringedal@hvl.no 

2) Associate Professor Therese B. Sjursen, assistant department leader

phone: +47 97 14 46 69 , e-mail: Therese.Berge.Sjursen@hvl.no 


Om arbeidsgiveren:

With about 17,500 students, Western Norway University of Applied Sciences is one of the largest higher education institutions in Norway. A broad range of academic programmes are offered at Bachelor, Master and PhD levels, spread out on five campuses Førde, Sogndal, Bergen, Stord og Haugesund.

Our ambition is to build stronger and more solid academic and research environments that will interact nationally and internationally. The aim is to become a recognized actor on the international higher education arena. Increased international cooperation and engagement in externally funded projects will work towards this goal.

The Department of Computer Science, Electrical Engineering and Mathematical Sciences has a strong academic and research environment, offering programmes at bachelor’s, master’s and PhD levels. The department has around 1,100 students and more than 120 staff members, and plays a key role in advancing technologies for digitalisation and the green transition.

We offer education across our campuses in Førde, Bergen and Haugesund, with six study programmes in computer science and electrical engineering, and teaching contributions in mathematics, statistics and physics.

The department hosts active research groups in areas such as software engineering, artificial intelligence, robotics, human-computer interaction and sensor networks, and collaborates closely with industry and public sector partners.

title: Founding Business Development Representative
description:
Who we are looking for

As our Founding Business Development Representative (BDR), you'll be the engine behind our sales pipeline - the first Birdsview person many prospects talk to. You'll open doors across Europe and beyond, working closely with our sales team to turn interest into qualified opportunities.

Birdsview - Prolonging the lifetime of the built world

Birdsview is a Norwegian technology company on a mission to change the way we preserve critical infrastructure to ensure a more sustainable and secure future.

Infrastructure is one of society’s most important assets. It includes the buildings we live in, the bridges we cross and the power grid that provides us with electricity. These structures are aging rapidly, and solutions that help preserve and secure critical infrastructure are now needed more than ever.

Birdsview's state-of-the-art technology combines radar (GPR), lidar, and AI to visualize what’s inside structures without destructive interventions. This allows for efficient and cost-effective inspection and monitoring of our most precious infrastructures - and enables clear, user-friendly visualizations that enhance understanding, extend asset lifespan, and promote material reuse - ultimately reducing costs and CO₂ emissions.

We are 17 people, we have customers in 9 countries, and we raised NOK 40.5 million from leading Nordic VC's to scale internationally.

About the job and why it matters

Much of concrete inspection today still relies on manual methods and fragmented, ageing non-destructive testing (NDT) equipment. You will help structural engineers, contractors, surveying specialists, and asset owners see clearly what is hidden inside the concrete. New critical data, faster inspections, and real cost savings are why they want our technology in their daily projects.

As a Founding BDA, you will be the engine behind our international growth. The role is to reach the right prospects, understand the problems they face, and show them what our technology does. You will build target account lists in HubSpot, make cold calls, drive LinkedIn and email outreach, and book qualified meetings for our sales team. This is a foundational role in a newly established sales team, where you will have a direct impact on our strategy, processes, and success.

  • Build the target list
    Research accounts across Europe and North America, and find the people who actually make the decision.

  • Run outbound
    Personalised outreach by phone, email and LinkedIn - plus follow-up on inbound leads and contacts from conferences.

  • Qualify and book
    Qualify opportunities, book meetings for the sales team, and keep our CRM clean enough that we can see what works.

  • Know the product and the market
    Deeply enough to have real conversations, not scripted ones.

  • Sharpen the message
    Feed back what you hear from prospects so marketing can build on it.

What we're looking for

  • Hunger and dedication to win.

  • Clear writing, thoughtful research, and confidence on the phone.

  • Outbound experience in SaaS, tech or another B2B role is a plus, not a requirement. Able to build pipeline yourself.

  • Organised and self-driven.

  • Comfortable working in a CRM. We use HubSpot.

  • At home where the process is still being figured out, you're helping figuring it out.

  • Fluent in English. Norwegian, German, Spanish or French is a strong plus given where our customers are.

Why this is interesting

  • Top-tier colleagues
    Work alongside leading people in a supportive and ambitious team culture, with regular social events and company trips.

  • Build it yourself
    Be a foundational member, directly shaping our international sales strategy and playbook.

  • Room to grow
    We're building the commercial team right now. What you own in a year depends on what you build in the first six months.

  • Impact
    Make a tangible impact on preserving critical infrastructure and fostering a circular economy.

  • Compensation
    Competitive salary, commission, and equity - become an owner.

  • Location
    Work in Bergen or Oslo with a fast-moving, hands-on team. Excellent working facilities at StartupLab centrally located in both cities.

View the full details for the job here.

title: Associate Professor (100 %, three years) in snow science / snow avalanches
employer: UNIVERSITETET I TROMSØ - NORGES ARKTISKE UNIVERSITET UIT CAMPUS TROMSØ
description:
The position

We are seeking a three-year fixed-term Associate Professor with a focus on snow science at the Department of Geosciences at The Faculty of Science and Technology, UiT the Arctic University of Norway. The position is attached to the Solid Earth Science, Mineral Resources and Geohazards scientific group.

Tromsø is a vibrant Arctic city surrounded by dramatic mountains, fjords and accessible wilderness — an exceptional living laboratory for snow and mountain research. The region offers year-round opportunities for fieldwork, easy access to skiing and mountaineering, and outstanding nature experiences (midnight sun in summer, northern lights in winter). We value work-life balance and outdoor culture here, which many researchers find inspiring for both research and personal life.

The workplace is at UiT in Tromsø. You must be able to start in the position in Tromsø within a reasonable time after receiving the offer.


The department

The Department of Geosciences has currently 16 permanent scientific staff positions, 21 post-doctoral fellows and researchers, 24 PhD students and 15 technical/administrative positions. The Department includes three scientific groups: (1) Solid Earth Science, Mineral Resources and Geohazards group, (2) Sedimentary Systems, Paleoclimates and Environments group, and (3) Geophysics, Glaciology and Oceanography group. It also hosts the Centre of Excellence iC3: Centre for ice, Cryosphere, Carbon and Climate . The Department is also a member of iEarth - Centre for Integrated Earth Science Education. We offer courses at all levels from bachelor to PhD studies and hosts approximately 150 students.

Over the last decade, the department has strategically built up expertise and research and education activities in geohazards. Geohazards is now a key focus area for the department, with established networks, ongoing projects and ambitions to further expand capabilities in snow science, avalanches and related processes. Earlier work has focused on rock slopes, slush flows, wet snow avalanches, climate adaptation and hazard/runout modelling. We would like to develop this research direction. The position benefits from active connections to the Department of Physics and Technology, Department of Technology and Safety and the Center for Avalanche Research and Education (CARE), and interdisciplinary research is encouraged to strengthen UiT’s position as a driver of Arctic knowledge, such as incorporating elements of psychology, preparedness and climate research.


The position’s field of research/field of work

The successful candidate is expected to:

  • Conduct high-quality research that strengthens UiT’s snow science portfolio within the snow science and geohazards thematic area. Research may also be interdisciplinary, and a connection with CARE and other UiT institutes is encouraged.
  • Teach undergraduate and advanced graduate courses, as well as participate in teaching of the field courses organized by the scientific group. The successful candidate will be expected to fulfil basic pedagogical competence within two years.
  • Supervise students at all levels, including MSc and PhD students.
  • Build external networks and represent the department at meetings, conferences and community outreach events.
  • Respond to media enquiries within your field.
  • Collaborate with colleagues to secure external funding and contribute to establishing permanent snow science capability at UiT.

It is expected that the participant will participate in disseminating research to a wider public. 


Contact

Further information about the position and UiT is available by contacting

Associate Professor Louise Daines-Vick, phone + 47 90 47 30 83, email: louise.m.vick@uit.no

Professor/Head of Department (interim) Anders Schomacker, phone + 47 95 52 34 64, email: anders.schomacker@uit.no


Qualifications

For this three-year fixed-term position as Associate Professor with a focus on snow science the applicants

  • must have a PhD in geosciences, physics, mathematics or a closely related field and a documented publication record in snow science and/or related geohazards. 
  • must have experience in, and a strong dedication to, field-based research and navigating snowy terrain. A track record or commitment to acquisition of external funding is desired.  The research should complement the existing research strengths within the fields of the Solid Earth Science, Mineral Resources and Geohazards scientific group, which includes the field of geohazards. 
  • must have an ability to communicate effectively in English. 
  • documented pedagogical competence. All applicants for teaching and research positions shall document their pedagogical competence. You must have acquired basic competence for teaching and supervision at higher education level. This includes basic skills in planning, conducting, evaluating and developing teaching and guidance. Those who do not meet the requirements for pedagogical competence upon employment will be required to meet them within two years.
  • Norwegian language skills: The position requires proficiency in a Scandinavian language equivalent to level B2 in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages (CEFR). New employees who do not fulfill the language criteria by appointment are required, within three years, to demonstrate sufficient proficiency in Norwegian or another Scandinavian language. Arrangements will be made to facilitate the completion of Norwegian courses.
  • personal suitability: Our working culture is important to us. We will emphasize the applicants motivation for the position and personal suitability. We are looking for candidates who display the following:
    • Collegial team player, ability to cooperate and communicate well with other members of staff and contribute to a good working environment.
    • Strong networking skills, ability to collaborate and conduct scientific leadership
    • Interest in strategy and strategic development of the department.
    • Good communication skills and ability to engage with academic, stakeholder and public audiences.

The applicants should have expertise in one or several aspects of snow avalanches and geohazards. Research approaches may include, for example, remote sensing, numerical and physical modelling, laboratory experiments, and field measurements on snow, slush, debris, or mixed materials. 

At UiT we put emphasis on the quality, relevance and significance of the research work and not on where the work is published, in accordance with the principles of The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment (DORA).


Pedagogical competence

All applicants for teaching and research positions must document their educational competence in their application.

Those who do not meet the requirements for pedagogical competence upon employment will be required to meet them within two years. UiT offers courses in educational competence to employees.

You must have acquired basic competence for teaching and supervision at university and college level.This entails basic skills in planning, implementing, evaluating and developing teaching and supervision. 

See how to document educational competence: About the pedagogical portfolio - Result  (English guide at the bottom of the page)


We offer
  • A stimulating international research environment within the geohazards theme and opportunities for collaboration across UiT.
  • Support for career development, supervision of students and external funding applications
  • Access to university research infrastructure, administrative and technical support, and professional development (mentoring, courses and workshops)
  • You will join a thriving geosciences environment with active projects, a strong student cohort and close interdisciplinary collaboration. You will have access to relevant laboratory and field equipment, opportunities to participate in and lead field campaigns, and support for outreach and stakeholder engagement
  • Allocated funds to support your research, travel and equipment needs
  • Good welfare arrangements for employees
  • Good arrangements for pension, insurance and loans in the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund
  • Access to the department cabin Heiahytta for a reasonable rental fee
  • If you have to relocate to Tromsø then the Faculty of Science and Technology may reimburse your moving costs. Further details regarding this matter will be made available if you receive an offer from us.

 

Norwegian health policy aims to ensure that everyone, irrespective of their personal finances and where they live, has access to good health and care services of equal standard. As an employee you will become member of the National Insurance Scheme which also include health care services.


Work- and salary conditions 

The successful candidate must be willing to get involved in the ongoing development of their department and the university as a whole.

The allocation of working hours is flexible and allocated on a case-by-case basis. In general, Associate Professors will spend an equal amount of time on teaching and research and development work after time spent on other duties has been deducted. As a norm, the time resources spent on administrative duties constitutes 5 % for academic staff. 

The remuneration for Associate Professor is in accordance with the State salary scale code 1011, with a gross annual salary ranging from NOK 700000,-  to 900000,- in a 100 % position. In special cases, a higher salary may be considered. 

As a state employee, you have one of the best pension schemes available. For more information see: spk.no.


Application

The application must include: 

  • Cover letter including a short description of interests and reasons for applying for the position  
  • CV containing a complete overview of education, experience and professional work 
  • Diplomas, diploma supplements and transcripts (all degrees, in original language and translated) 
  • Letter(s) of recommendation if applicable
  • Two references with contact details 
  • Documented pedagogical competence. Brief description of teaching philosophy/documentation of educational competence in the form of a pedagogical map or course certificate of completed university pedagogical basic competence such as UNIPED 100 at UiT or equivalent from other universities 
  • A list of your academic production 
  • Description of your academic production, stating which works you consider most important 
  • Academic works, up to ten. The doctoral thesis is regarded as one work. 
  • Documentation of English proficiency.  

Proficiency in the English language can be documented in the following ways: 

  • Diploma from a Norwegian upper secondary school with both spoken and written English (140 hours) 
  • TOEFL (Test of English as a Foreign Language) 
  • IELTS (International English Testing Service) 
  • Completed university degree in the field of English language or literature 
  • One year of completed university studies in Australia, Canada, Ireland, New Zealand, the UK or USA, for which English was the language of instructions. 

Documentation has to be in English or a Scandinavian language. The application and submitted documents must be sent electronically via www.jobbnorge.no 


Assessment

The applicants will be assessed by an expert committee. The committee's mandate is to undertake an assessment of the applicants' qualifications on the basis of the written material presented by the applicants, and the detailed description drawn up for the position.

The applicants who are assessed as best qualified will be called to an interview. The interview shall among other things, aim to clarify the applicants personal suitability for the position and motivations. A trial lecture may also be held.


General information

The appointment is made in accordance with State regulations and guidelines at UiT. At our website, you will find more information for applicants.

The engagement is to be made in accordance with the acts relating to Control of the Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology. Candidates who by assessment of the application and attachment are seen to conflict with the criteria in the latter law will be prohibited from recruitment.

After the appointment you must assume that there may be changes in the area of work.

More information about moving to Norway and working at UiT: http://uit.no/mobility

​According to the Norwegian Freedom and Information Act (Offentleglova) information about the applicant may be included in the public applicant list, also in cases where the applicant has requested non-disclosure.

In case of discrepancies between the Norwegian and the English version of this description, the Norwegian version takes precedence.

title: Founding Growth Marketer
description:
Who we are looking for

We're looking for a Founding Growth Marketer to build Birdsview's growth engine from the ground up, the person who turns "we have a great product" into a steady flow of qualified pipeline. AI first person.

Birdsview - Prolonging the lifetime of the built world

Birdsview is a Norwegian technology company on a mission to change the way we preserve critical infrastructure to ensure a more sustainable and secure future.

Infrastructure is one of society’s most important assets. It includes the buildings we live in, the bridges we cross and the power grid that provides us with electricity. These structures are aging rapidly, and solutions that help preserve and secure critical infrastructure are now needed more than ever.

Birdsview's state-of-the-art technology combines radar (GPR), lidar, and AI to visualize what’s inside structures without destructive interventions. This allows for efficient and cost-effective inspection and monitoring of our most precious infrastructures - and enables clear, user-friendly visualizations that enhance understanding, extend asset lifespan, and promote material reuse - ultimately reducing costs and CO₂ emissions.

We are 17 people, we have customers in 9 countries, and we raised NOK 40.5 million from leading Nordic VC's to scale internationally.

About the job and why it matters

Much of concrete inspection today still relies on manual methods and fragmented, ageing non-destructive testing (NDT) equipment. You will help structural engineers, contractors, surveying specialists, and asset owners see clearly what is hidden inside the concrete. New critical data, faster inspections, and real cost savings are why they want our technology in their daily projects.

As a Founding Growth Marketer, you will be the engine of our international growth. The role is hands-on: you'll use AI tools to build and test campaigns across channels, turn technical value into content that resonates with engineers and asset owners, run experiments to find what actually converts, and hand qualified leads to our sales team. This is a foundational role in a newly formed marketing function, where you will have a direct impact on our strategy, processes, and success.

    Set up tracking, reporting, and analytics to measure performance, identify effective strategies, and drive continuous improvement.

  • Make the technical obvious

What we're looking for

  • AI-first, systematic and test-driven. You run experiments, read the data, and a campaign that flops doesn't slow you down.

  • Proven ability to build and run a complete growth engine: lead generation, content, paid campaigns, organic channels.

  • Skills in setting up tracking, reporting and analytics, so performance is measured rather than asserted.

  • Experience developing, testing and refining positioning and messaging, in collaboration with sales and leadership.

  • 1–3 years of experience in B2B growth or marketing, ideally in a startup or scale-up. Hands-on and results-oriented, this is a building role.

  • Fluent English; Norwegian is an advantage.

  • Based in Bergen or Oslo, or willing to relocate.

Why this is interesting

    Work alongside leading people in a supportive and ambitious team culture, with regular social events and company trips.

title: PhD Research Fellow in Bioinformatics and Computational Biology
description:
About the position

We invite applications for a position as PhD Research Fellow in bioinformatics and computational biology available at the Department of Clinical Molecular Biology (EpiGen), Campus Ahus, University of Oslo.

 

The preferred starting date is as soon as possible.

 

The fellowship period is three years and is free of any teaching obligations. No one can be appointed for more than one PhD Research Fellowship period at the University of Oslo.

 

The position is based at the Department of Clinical Molecular Biology (EpiGen; https://epigenahuscom.wordpress.com/) at the University of Oslo, Ahus Campus, Lørenskog. EpiGen is a joint research unit established by the University of Oslo (UiO) and Akershus University Hospital (Ahus). It is actively involved in several major national research initiatives and provides an outstanding research environment with state-of-the-art laboratories and dedicated research facilities. The position is funded by the Research Council of Norway.

 

 

The successful candidate will join an interdisciplinary team of molecular biologists, bioinformaticians, physicists, and pathologists to develop a biophysically interpretable machine learning model that integrates diverse biological data—including transcription factor (TF)–DNA interactions, epigenetic features, and three-dimensional (3D) genome organization—to identify functional long-range gene regulatory interactions in cancer. The candidate will work with researchers at UiO, Ahus, and Oslo University Hospital (OUS), as well as by international collaborators in the United States. The research conducted during the appointment is expected to culminate in a PhD thesis submitted to the University of Oslo.

 

We seek a highly motivated candidate with a strong background in molecular biology, human genetics/genomics, data mining, machine learning, and computational programming. The ideal candidate will hold a Master's degree in bioinformatics or computational biology. Applicants with an MSc in physics, computer science, applied mathematics, or statistics are also encouraged to apply, provided they can demonstrate a strong interest and aptitude for learning molecular biology and human genetics.


More about the position

The project aims to develop novel computational methods and tools for predicting functional non-coding mutations in the cancer genome. These methods will integrate diverse sources of information, including the biophysical principles of protein–DNA interactions, the genetic and epigenetic features of DNA sequences, and the three-dimensional (3D) organization of the genome and its regulatory landscape. A particular focus will be on integrating multi-omics data generated from single-cell experiments to improve both predictive accuracy and biological interpretability.

 

The PhD research fellow will primarily focus on developing data mining methods such as network analysis in 3D genome regulation that integrate diverse biological information, including transcription factor (TF)–DNA interactions, epigenetic features, and 3D genome organization, to identify functional non-coding mutations and their targets in long-distance regions. Subsequently, the predictions will be validated in cancer by using both in vivo and in vitro experimental data.

 

Depending on the candidate's qualifications and the progress of the project, there may be an opportunity to undertake a 3–6-month research visit to the laboratory of one of our international collaborators in the United States. This visit will provide advanced training in computational approaches for studying single-cell 3D genome regulation and further strengthen the international collaboration.


What skills are important in this role?

Candidates for the PhD fellowships will be expected to be in the upper segment of their class with respect to academic credentials.

 

Required qualifications:

  • To be admitted to the PhDprogramme at the University ofOslo, an applicant musthave a five-year master'sdegree or equivalent studiesthat the faculty have recognised as forminga sufficient basisfor admission.
  • The facultiesmay stipulate additional admission requirements.
  • To be employed as aPhD ResearchFellow, admission toa doctoral program is required,or a binding agreementfor admission must be in place. Normally, one must apply foradmission to a Ph.D. program within3 months after thestart of the research project leading tothe Ph.D. degree.
  • Good written and oral Englishproficiency.
  • Master's degree in bioinformatics or computational biology. Applicants with an MSc in physics, computer science, applied mathematics, or statistics are also encouraged to apply, provided they can demonstrate a strong interest and aptitude for learning molecular biology and the human genome.
  • Documented knowledge of statistical theory and methods, data mining, and machine learning methods.
  • Documented shell script, R, Python, and C programming skills. 
  • Documented experience in big data analysis.
  • Documented experience in high-throughput sequencing data analysis.

 

Language requirement:

  • Good written and oral English proficiency.
  • English requirements for applicants from outside of EU/ EEA countries and exemptions from the requirements:
  • https://www.mn.uio.no/english/research/phd/regulations/regulations.html#toc8

 

Grade requirements:

  • The average grade point for the course in the Bachelor's degree must be C or better (Norwegian educational system)
  • The average grade point for the course in the Master's degree must be B or better in the Norwegian educational system
  • The Master's thesis must have the grade B or better in the Norwegian educational system

 

 

 

Personal qualities 

  • Academic and personal ability to finish tasks on time
  • Ability to work either independently or collaboratively in an interdisciplinary team
  • Self-motivated to learn, easily adapted to new tasks, and interested in solving challenging scientific problems.
  • Good communication skills and openness to new perspectives

 

Desired qualifications

  • Experience with ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq/scATAC-seq, RNA-seq/scRNA-seq, WGS, WGBS, or Hi-C data analysis.
  • Experience in computational genome studies (e.g., TF-DNA interactions, gene networks, DNA mutations, and histone modifications). 
  • Experience with integrated multi-omics data analysis.aaa

 

Employment in the position is basedon a comprehensive assessment of allqualification requirements applicable tothe position, including 

personal qualifications.


We need different perspectives in our work 

UiO is an open and internationally oriented comprehensive university that strives to be an inclusive and diverse workplace and academic environment. You can read more about UiO’s work on equality, inclusion, and diversity at uio.no.

We fulfill our mission most effectively when we draw upon our variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives. We are looking for great colleagues—could you be the next one?

We will provide appropriate accommodations should you need them. Relevant adjustments may include modifications to working hours, task adaptations, digital, technical, or physical adjustments, or other practical measures.

If you have an immigrant background, a disability, or CV gaps, we encourage you to indicate this in the job application portal. We always invite at least one qualified candidate from each group for an interview. In this context, disability is defined as an applicant who identifies as having a disability that requires workplace or employment-related accommodations. For more details about the requirements, please refer to the Employer portal (Norwegian).

The selections made in the job application portal are used for anonymized statistics that all state employers include in their annual reports.

More information about gender equality initiatives at UiO can be found here.

We hope you will apply for the position with us. 


We offer
  • Exciting and meaningfultasks in an organization with an important societal mission, contributing toknowledge development, education, andenlightenment that promote sustainable, fair, andknowledge-based societal development.
  • Committed colleagues in a good working environment. A pleasantand stimulatingwork environment.
  • Good welfare schemes.
  • Opportunity of up to 1.5hours a week of exercise during working hours. A workplace with good development and careeropportunities.
  • Membership in the Statens Pensjonskasse, which is one of Norway's best pension schemes,with beneficialmortgages and good insurance schemes.
  • Salary in the position as DoctoralResearch Fellow, position code1017 in the salary range of NOK 550 800 -600 000, depending oncompetence and experience. From the salary, 2 percent isdeducted in statutory contributions to theState Pension Fund.
  • Read more about the benefitsof working in thepublic sector at Employer Portal.

Application

Your application should include:

  • Application cover letter (statement of motivation and research interests) 
  • CV (summarizing education, positions and academic work - scientific publications)
  • A copy of the Master's thesis, a list of publications and academic works (maximum 5) that you wish to be considered by the committee
  • Certified copies of the original Bachelor and Master's degree diploma and the transcripts of records
  • Documentation of English proficiency if applicable
  • Contact information for at least 3 references (name, relation to the candidate, institutional email address and telephone number)

Your CV must be entered in Jobbnorge’s CV form and cannot be submitted only as an attachment. This requirement is intended to ensure correct documentation and record-keeping in accordance with the Public Administration Act, Section 15.

Application with attachments must be submitted via our recruitment system Jobbnorge, click "Apply for this job".

When applying for the position, we ask you to retrieve your education results from Vitnemålsportalen.no. If your education results are not available through Vitnemålsportalen, we ask you to upload copies of your transcripts or grades. Please note that all documentation must be in English or a Scandinavian language.


Contact information 

For further information, please contact:

  • Junbai Wang, junbai.wang@medisin.uio.no

 

For questions regarding Jobbnorge, please

  • Maren Retterstøl Olaisen, HR advisor, m.r.olaisen@medisin.uio.no

Place of service:

Department of Clinical Molecular Biology (EpiGen)

University of Oslo, Ahus campus

1748 Lørenskog


General information

Please note that we are unable to add documentation after the application deadline. As the deadline applies equally to all applicants, this policy ensures equal treatment throughout the recruitment process. If you experience difficulties uploading documents in Jobbnorge, please contact their customer service: Phone: +47 75 54 22 20 or Email: support@grade.com 

The primary method of communication throughout the process will be e-mails and messages through the recruitment system Jobbnorge. When you receive a notification of a message in Jobbnorge, please log in to read it, as it may be important.

The best qualified candidates will invited for interviews. 

Applicant lists can be published in accordance with Norwegian Freedom of Information Act § 25. When you apply for a position with us, your name will appear on the public applicant list. It is possible to request to be excluded from this list. You must justify why you want an exemption from publication and we will then decide whether we can grant your request. If we cannot, you will hear from us.

Please refer to Regulations for the Act on universities and colleges chapter 3 (Norwegian), Guidelines concerning appointment to recruitment positions at UiO and Regulations for the degree of Philosophiae Doctor (PhD) at the University of Oslo.

The University of Oslo has a transfer agreement with all employees to secure the rights to all research results and related intellectual property.


Om arbeidsgiveren:

The University of Oslo is Norway’s oldest and highest ranked educational and research institution, with 26 500 students and 7 200 employees. With its broad range of academic disciplines and internationally recognised research communities, UiO is an important contributor to society.

The Institute of Clinical Medicine (Klinmed) is one of three institutes under the Faculty. Klinmed is responsible for the Faculty's educational and research activities at Oslo University Hospital and Akershus University Hospital. With about 900 employees spread over approximately 425 man-labour years, Klinmed is the university's largest institute. Our activities follow the clinical activity at the hospitals and are spread across a number of geographical areas.

The project aims to develop a biophysically interpretable machine learning framework that integrates diverse biological data—including transcription factor (TF)–DNA interactions, epigenomic features, and three-dimensional (3D) genome organization—to identify functional long-range gene regulatory interactions in cancer. The postdoctoral researcher will collaborate closely with students, PhD candidates, researchers, and national and international partners. The work is expected to result in high-quality scientific publications as well as broadly applicable computational resources, such as open-source software and bioinformatics tools.

 

We seek a highly motivated and ambitious researcher with a strong background in molecular biology, human genetics/genomics, bioinformatics, machine learning, data mining, and computational programming, including software or package development. The ideal candidate will hold a PhD in bioinformatics or computational biology. Applicants with a PhD in related disciplines, such as computer science, physics, applied mathematics, statistics, or a closely related quantitative field, are also encouraged to apply, provided they demonstrate a strong interest in and commitment to applying computational methods to molecular biology and human genetics/genomics.


More about the position

The project aims to develop novel computational methods and tools for predicting functional non-coding mutations in the cancer genome. These methods will integrate diverse sources of biological information, including the biophysical principles governing protein–DNA interactions, the genetic and epigenetic features of DNA sequences, and the three-dimensional (3D) organization of the genome and its regulatory landscape. A particular emphasis will be placed on integrating multi-omics data generated from single-cell experiments to enhance both predictive accuracy and biological interpretability.


The Postdoctoral Research Fellow will primarily focus on developing a biophysically interpretable machine learning framework that integrates multiple layers of biological information, including transcription factor (TF)–DNA interactions, epigenetic features, and 3D genome organization, to identify functional long-range gene regulatory interactions from in vivo data. The candidate will also be involved in the validation of predictions from cancer genomes.
 

Throughout the fellowship, the Postdoctoral Research Fellow will be supported by a structured career development plan. This may include opportunities to teach and supervise bioinformatics students, present research at international conferences, and undertake research visits to leading international laboratories. The fellowship is designed to equip the candidate with the scientific expertise, professional skills, and international research experience needed to pursue a competitive research career within or beyond academia. The University of Oslo (UiO) is committed to supporting the Fellow's career development by providing ongoing mentoring and access to career guidance throughout the postdoctoral appointment.


About the position

You must have
To be appointed as a postdoctoral fellow, a doctoral degree is required.

  • Good written and oral English proficiency.
  • Applicants must hold a degree equivalent to a Norwegian doctoral degree in bioinformatics, computational biology, or other relevant research fields to the project. The doctoral dissertation must be submitted for evaluation by the application deadline. Only applicants with an approved doctoral thesis and public defense are eligible for appointment.
  • Personal suitability and motivation for the project.
  • Documented knowledge of statistical theory and methods, data mining, and machine learning methods.
  • Documented shell script, R, Python, and C programming skills.
  • Documented experience in big data analysis and computational tool/package development.
  • Documented experience in high-throughput sequencing data analysis or computational genome regulation.
     

Personal qualities
 

  • Academic and personal ability to finish tasks on time
  • Ability to work either independently or collaboratively in an interdisciplinary team
  • Self-motivated to learn, easily adapted to new tasks, and interested in solving challenging scientific problems.

  • Good communication skills and openness to new perspectives

     

Desired qualifications
Experience with ChIP-seq, ATAC-seq/scATAC-seq, RNA-seq/scRNA-seq, WGS, WGBS, or Hi-C data analysis
Experience in computational genome studies (e.g., TF-DNA interactions, gene networks, DNA mutations, and histone modifications).
Experience with integrated multi-omics data analysis and software/package tool development

 

Employment in the position is based on a comprehensive assessment of all qualification requirements applicable to the position, including personal qualifications.

description:
Vil du bidra til at flere barn, unge og voksne får oppleve gleden av aktivitet og friluftsliv – helt gratis?
Drammen kommune søker engasjerte og selvstendige tilkallingsvikarer til våre BUA-utstyrssentraler i Mjøndalen, på Fjell og ved vår nye BUA på Åssiden. 
Vi ser spesielt etter deg som har interesse for ski, friluftsliv og aktivitet, og som trives med å møte mennesker i alle aldre.

Om BUA
BUA er en gratis utlånsordning for sports- og fritidsutstyr som alle kan benytte akkurat som et bibliotek. Gjennom BUA ønsker Drammen kommune å bidra til:
- bedre folkehelse
- mindre sosiale forskjeller
- mer bærekraftig forbruk
- hele familien ut på tur

Hos oss kan alle låne utstyr til aktivitet og friluftsliv, uavhengig av økonomi.
BUA skal være et inkluderende møtested og et naturlig utgangspunkt.

Om stillingen
Som servicemedarbeider i BUA er du ansiktet utad for både BUA og Drammen kommune. Du møter mennesker med ulike behov og bidrar til gode opplevelser, enten det er en familie som skal på tur eller ungdom som ønsker å prøve skiutstyr for første gang.
Arbeidet foregår hovedsakelig på ettermiddag og kveld. I enkelte perioder, særlig i vintersesongen, må det påregnes høy aktivitet og stor pågang.
Det forventes at du kan jobbe på alle BUA-utstyrssentralene i Drammen. Dette vil si Mjøndalen, Svelvik, Fjell og Åssiden.

NB: Til denne stillingen ønsker vi ikke søknadsbrev, men heller at du svarer på konkrete spørsmål vi har laget. Svarene på spørsmålene sammen med CV vil bli brukt til vurdering av hvilke søkere som innehar de kvalifikasjoner vi er på utkikk etter og hvem blant disse som blir innkalt til intervju.

Søknader vurderes fortløpende. Aktuelle kandidater kan bli invitert til intervju før søknadsfristens utløp, så vi oppfordrer interesserte til å søke så snart som mulig.

  • Sørge for orden, system og god oversikt i utlånssystemet
  • Vedlikeholde, rengjøre og utføre enklere reparasjoner av utstyr
  • Følge opp utlån og purringer
  • Besvare henvendelser på telefon og e-post

  • Bidra på arrangementer og aktivitetsdager gjennom året
  • Dele kunnskap og bidra til opplæring av deltakere i arbeidspraksis
Kvalifikasjoner

Krav

  • Du har fylt 16 år
  • Du har gode muntlige norskkunnskaper
  • Du behersker digitale verktøy og systemer

Ønskelige kvalifikasjoner

  • Erfaring fra friluftsliv, ski, idrett eller annen aktivitet
  • Interesse for og kunnskap om sports- og fritidsutstyr
  • Erfaring fra servicearbeid, butikk eller kundebehandling

Personlige egenskaper

Vi ser etter deg som:

  • trives i et arbeidsmiljø med høyt tempo

I vår fysioterapiseksjon er vi i overkant av 20 svært kompetente og driftige fysioterapeuter.
Seksjonens fysioterapeuter jobber til daglig i hovedsak med inneliggende pasienter. Vi behandler en rekke ulike pasientkategorier på intensivavdelingene, sengeposter og i treningssal. Hovedvekten av våre pasienter er:

  • Hjerte: hjerte-/karkirurgi, hjertetransplantasjon og kardiologiske pasienter
  • Lunge: lungetransplantasjon og lungeoperasjoner
  • ØNH: voksne pasienter operert for cancer
  • Gastro/transplantasjon: gastrokirurgi, gastromedisin, nyretransplanterte, levertransplanterte
  • Pasienter på sengepost for Blodsykdommer og Infeksjon

Hverdagen vår er varierende, størstedelen av våre behandlinger er på sengepost, men vi har også noe poliklinisk drift i intensiv- og bløderpoliklinikk. Vi er svært opptatt av faglig utvikling og setter fokus på evidensbasert tilgang gjennom kontinuerlig forbedringsarbeid. Vi er stolte av å ha et åpent og inkluderende arbeidsmiljø, som gjør at vi arbeider godt sammen, både internt og ut mot sengepostene.

Vi søker deg som ønsker å jobbe med våre pasientgrupper, og som har erfaring fra spesialisthelsetjenesten. Det er ønskelig at du har erfaring med intensivfysioterapi og er godt kjent med lungefysioterapi til ulike pasientgrupper.

 

Det er mulighet for forlengelse i enkelte vikariater. Ved intern ansettelse kan vikariater at ulik varighet og stillingsprosent bli ledig.

Intervjuer gjennomføres fortløpende.
